messages:
sara: FYI customer tom_acme reporting quantized endpoint (acme-prod-quant v3) is consistently slower than their FP16 variant and sometimes returns lower-quality outputs. They see p95 jump from ~220ms to ~620ms. Filing now so eng can triage.

michael: Thanks. Can you paste the endpoint name + model + example request payload? Any repro script?

sara: Endpoint: acme-prod-quant-v3, Model: redwood-rlhf-13b-quant4, Customer sample: single-turn chat, prompt length ~40 tokens. They hit it with batch size=1 from their web UI. Repro curl they used: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"acme-prod-quant-v3","input":"Write a short product summary: ...","max_tokens":150}'
```

anjali: I'm looking at recent profiler traces from the dedicated pool for that endpoint. Early sign: calibration phase is triggering per-request on cold KV cache and uses a CPU-bound calibration routine that blocks the fast CUDA kernel path. Also kernel selector is falling back to a generic INT4 slow path for sequence lengths <= 64 due to a heuristic we recently changed. Pasting a trimmed perf sample: 
```
Perf sample (request):
  total: 580ms
  cuda_infer kernels: 180ms
  cpu calibration step: 240ms  <-- dominates
  kv-cache misses & warmup: 90ms
  scheduling overhead: 70ms
Top kernels: quant_kernel_4bit_generic (slow) 120ms, fast_quant_kernel_4bit_fused 60ms (not used)
```

michael: Interesting — so two things: (1) calibration is running on hot path per request; (2) kernel selector is choosing slow generic kernel for short sequences. Any recent commits to calibration or selector heuristics?

anjali: Yes, yesterday we merged PR that defers precomputed calibration tables if the sample distribution differs > 5% (to avoid quality regressions). That logic incorrectly marks most short prompt requests as "distribution changed" which triggers full calibration on CPU. Also a threshold tweak in kernel selector favors safe generic kernels when batch size < 2.

jess: Can we repro locally? I can spin a small repro harness against the same model artifacts. If we can reproduce, we can test two mitigations: force use of precomputed calibration (skip dynamic cal) and force kernel selector to prefer fused fast kernel for these geometry shapes.

anjali: Repro steps that matched customer: run single-request loop (batch=1) with prompt 40 tokens for 100 iterations against dedicated pool instance. I attached command we used: 
```bash
for i in {1..100}; do curl -sS -X POST $ENDPOINT -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -d '{"model":"acme-prod-quant-v3","input":"...","max_tokens":150}' >/dev/null; sleep 0.2; done
```
We saw p95 ~610ms same as customer.

michael: Great. Quick mitigation: can we push a routing rule to fall back to FP16 model variant for acme-prod-quant-v3 for any request where batch_size==1 until we push a proper fix? That should be low-risk and buy time. Also ask ops to pre-warm KV cache for their pool.

ops-bot: deploy: routing update queued for acme-prod-quant-v3 -> fp16 fallback for batch_size==1. Change ID: R-2026-891. ETA 15m.

jess: I tested two patches locally: (A) skip-dynamic-calibration flag (uses stored calibration table) reduces cpu calibration time from 240ms -> 10ms and end-to-end p95 -> 230ms; (B) adjust kernel selector threshold to allow fused fast kernel when seq_len<=64 and batch_size==1, gives p95 -> 260ms. Patch A looks safest.

anjali: Agree. Patch A also preserves output quality because stored tables were generated from customer workload during onboarding. We should run a small A/B on a subset of traffic first.

michael: Plan: 1) Ops will enable routing fallback to FP16 for batch_size==1 immediately (done). 2) Eng will enable skip-dynamic-calibration flag for acme pool on canary instances and monitor quality/regressions. 3) If stable, rollout to entire pool and then revert routing fallback. 4) Follow-up: fix kernel selector heuristic in next release.

ops-bot: routing update complete. Change ID R-2026-891 applied to acme-prod-pool. All traffic for batch_size==1 now goes to acme-prod-fp16-v3.

anjali: Canary results after enabling skip-dynamic-calibration on 2 nodes: p95 ~240ms, CPU time down to ~12ms, no obvious quality delta on our eval prompt set (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarities within noise).

tom_acme: Thanks team — latency is back to previous levels, customers seeing faster responses. Any ETA on full fix so we can stop routing to FP16?

michael: We'll monitor canary for 24 hours. If stable, we'll flip the pool (estimated within 8-12 hours). We'll also create a postmortem and a changelog note explaining the calibration gating bug.

jess: Follow-up action items: ENG-1257 (skip-dynamic-calib flag formalized + tests), ENG-1258 (kernel-selector threshold revert + unit tests), CS-4021 (customer comms + confirm quality metric windows).

anjali: I'll draft the customer-facing message proposing timeline and stating root cause (calibration gating bug + selector threshold change), plus that we restored performance via temporary FP16 routing and will revert once patched.

sara: I'll send the note to tom_acme and update the CS ticket. Thanks everyone. :tada:
